feature.title: Bass ink enhanced graphics
feature.request: we want to enhance the bass-ink visualization with support for the enhanced graphics. This can include any sort of additions that will make it visualy more stunning.  Branch from origin/main so you can see the shared toggle for enhanced graphics.  The goal here is to make bass-ink as visually stunning as possible, without losing the core of what the visualization does

problem.statement: bass-ink is a tempo-breathing point cloud that reforms on drops, flashes on kicks and sprays on bass hits, drawn through a fixed trails and bloom composer. The shared enhanced-graphics toggle (on origin/main, not yet in the local checkout) lets visualizers offer a richer look, but bass-ink does not opt in, so users who turn it on see nothing new here.
users: Viewers who turn on enhanced graphics on a capable machine and want bass-ink to look as stunning as possible
Viewers on standard mode or software renderers, who must see bass-ink exactly as today
evidence: context-brief.md: no enhanced or quality reference under app/ in this checkout; local main c03849a behind origin/main bd71db4
docs/plans/cubes-, trio-, dancer-enhanced-graphics: the agreed pattern (lazy chunk, toggle off unchanged, in-place swap, software fallback, reduced-motion damping)
bassInkPost.ts and docs/plans/bass-ink-post/contracts.md: existing composer and flash-safety rule

goals: With enhanced graphics on, bass-ink looks markedly richer (depth, glow, colour and texture) while staying recognisably the same piece: same formations, palette family and bass, kick and drop reactions
In both modes, the camera rotates gradually on a tilted orbit whose speed rises smoothly with the combined level of the three trio-color-wave bands (bass, mids, highs)
Enhanced mode holds about 60 fps at 1080p on a mid-range or integrated laptop GPU
Toggle off, and any software renderer, keep today's render path and passes; the only standard-mode change is the camera rotation
non_goals: Changing bass-ink's standard look beyond the camera rotation: controls defaults, formations, director and reaction timing stay
Changing the shared enhanced-graphics toggle, its storage or other visualizers' behaviour (trio-color-wave output must not change if band code is shared)
New audio analysis or rhythm-tracker changes; the rotation reuses trio-color-wave's band split and everything else reuses existing bass, kick and drop signals
Upgrading three.js or adding non-three dependencies
Making post effects follow the music in ways that add flashes (flash-safety rule stays)
success_metrics: Side-by-side review in npm run dev: enhanced is judged clearly more stunning and still recognisably bass-ink
Enhanced median frame time at or under about 16.7 ms at 1080p on the reference laptop GPU
scorecard:check passes and bass-ink reaction cells from debug:viz are unchanged within noise with enhanced off
Total JS gzip growth small and justified; entry chunk and Lighthouse on / unchanged
constraints: Follow the toggle contract as it exists on origin/main; implementation branches from origin/main
Enhanced code lives in a lazily loaded chunk; toggling swaps in place through the render hook, keeping the camera
No per-frame allocation; every GPU resource disposed; StrictMode double-mount safe
Flash safety (contracts.md:39): post strengths do not follow the music; at most 3 flashes per second as granted by BrightnessMix
Software renderers keep the plain path (bassInkPost.ts:78) even with enhanced on
three.js r186 pinned; addons from three/addons; bundle budget raise in the same PR with a reason
prefers-reduced-motion damps the rotation and any added motion

decisions.question: What rotates and how does it coexist with orbit controls?
decisions.answer: The camera, as in the dancer (dancingCharacterScene.ts:428-434, 481): the scene writes a tilted orbit pose only while the camera is locked (the default); unlocked hands the camera to the orbit controls and pauses the orbit; reset and relock zero the angle

decisions.question: What drives rotation speed?
decisions.answer: A trio-like split of bass-ink's own spectrum into bass, mids and highs with trio's default edges, its stateless helpers broken out into reusable shared code; the combined value, smoothed and rate-limited, maps to speed between a floor and a cap
decisions.rationale: User: trio-like, and break it out into reusable code if possible

decisions.question: Branching
decisions.answer: The implementation session branches from origin/main to get the toggle; this planning session only read the local checkout
decisions.rationale: Request says branch from origin/main; toggle API to be confirmed there

decisions.question: Risk class
decisions.rationale: Standard-mode motion changes and trio band code may be shared across visualizers

decisions.question: How does the rotation relate to Camera drift?
decisions.answer: Camera drift scales the orbit speed; drift 0 means no orbit
decisions.rationale: Keeps the still-view promise without a new control

decisions.question: Reduced motion
decisions.answer: Auto-orbit stopped, read live with matchMedia, passed into the orbit step
decisions.rationale: Matches the dancer, which does not rotate under reduced motion; one testable outcome

decisions.question: How does the toggle swap?
decisions.answer: Enhanced passes and shader variants are built once after the lazy load and toggled with enabled flags and a define; freed only on scene dispose
decisions.rationale: bassInkPost.ts:74-77 forbids switching render paths; avoids hitches and double frees

options.summary: Add a small pure camera-orbit module fed by a shared trio band-level helper, plus one lazy enhanced chunk that only swaps bloom/afterimage config and adds a static depth/colour-grade pass inside the existing composer.
approach: Extract trio-color-wave's band split into a pure function (bandLevels) imported by trio unchanged; add a snapshot test proving trio output identical (AC11).

Add cameraOrbit.ts: smooths combined level (asymmetric EMA), maps to angular speed floor..cap, integrates a yaw angle (monotonic, never reverses), fixed tilt; reduced-motion returns constant floor drift.
In useBassInkScene update: add orbit yaw as an offset composed with the existing user orbit/drift; skip when camera lock is on; reset view zeroes the offset. Same code in both modes (AC3, AC10).
Read the enhanced toggle from origin/main's useEnhancedGraphics; when on and not isSoftwareRenderer, dynamic-import bassInkEnhanced.ts.

bassInkEnhanced.ts adds to the existing composer in place: a fixed-strength extra bloom mip tint, a static vignette/chromatic grade pass, and a depth-fog uniform plus size/colour attenuation on existing point materials. No music-driven post values (AC7).
Toggle swaps passes through the render hook, keeps camera, disposes the added passes idempotently (AC4, AC8); load failure keeps standard with one warning.
Regenerate the standard baseline for rotation only, raise the size budget with a reason, append no probe columns except at the end.

options.summary: Extract a pure shared band-level function and a pure, unit-tested orbit controller (angle integration, never reverses), wire it into the camera in both modes, and add a lazily loaded enhanced post/shading chunk behind a strict fail-safe boundary with static, music-independent post strengths.
approach: Extract trio-color-wave's band split into a pure shared module (bandLevels) that trio imports unchanged; add a golden-output test proving trio output is identical (AC11).

Add orbitRotation.ts: pure state machine (smoothed combined level, speed = floor + (cap-floor)*smoothstep(level), angle += speed*dt, dt clamped, reduced-motion -> constant slow drift). Angle only integrates, so no reversal or jump.

In useBassInkScene, compose the orbit as an azimuth offset applied to the camera pose after OrbitControls/drift, using preallocated vectors; skip while camera lock is on; reset view zeroes the offset; the tilt is a fixed polar bias.

Add bassInkEnhanced.ts (dynamic import chunk): richer point shading (depth fade, soft sprite glow), extra static post (e.g. chromatic or vignette plus second bloom mip) with constant strengths, never audio-driven.

Render hook swaps standard and enhanced composers in place on toggle, keeping the camera; the enhanced build is gated by isSoftwareRenderer, and any load or build error falls back to standard with one warning.
Idempotent dispose of every target, pass, material and texture; StrictMode and cancelled-load guards (a late-resolving import is discarded if unmounted or toggled off).
Append telemetry columns only; raise the size budget with a reason; regenerate the standard baseline via the CI snapshot workflow for the rotation only.

options.summary: A viewer-first enhanced look (depth haze, soft-sprite glow, colour grading, light streak on kicks) that never strobes, plus a camera orbit that eases in and out so loudness feels like momentum, not a jolt, and every control still behaves as expected.
approach: Extract trio-color-wave's band split into a shared pure function (bandLevels.ts) re-imported by trio unchanged; its tests stay as-is. bass-ink calls it on the existing spectrum, with no new analysis.

orbitRotation.ts (pure, standard chunk): combined = bass+mids+highs, smoothed with a slow attack and slower release; speed = floor + (cap-floor)*smoothstep(combined). Integrate angle += speed*dt so it never reverses or jumps. Reduced motion pins speed to the floor, level-independent.

Apply as a yaw about the formation on a fixed tilt, composed over user orbit offset. Dragging pauses auto-yaw for about 1.5 s then resumes from the current angle with no snap. Lock stops it, reset view zeroes angle and the tilt pose, and camera drift stays additive.

enhanced/ lazy chunk (bassInkEnhanced.ts) built by the same render hook as bassInkPost. Adds depth-of-field style distance fade and size attenuation on points, a soft round-sprite glow, a static colour-grade and vignette pass, and a faint radial streak on kick whose brightness is capped by BrightnessMix. All post constants are fixed.

Swap in place on toggle: build the new path first, then switch and dispose the old one, keeping the camera. Chunk loading or failure keeps the standard look with one console.warn and no flicker. Software renderers skip the chunk.
Dev-only label shows the enhanced state in the existing telemetry; append-only probe columns carry angle and speed.
Raise the size budget with a stated reason; run debug:viz and scorecard:check.

design.overview: Two independent additions. (1) A camera auto-orbit in both modes, following the dancer: while the camera is locked, the scene writes a tilted orbit pose whose angular speed comes from a trio-like three-band split of bass-ink's own spectrum (combined level, smoothed and rate-limited), scaled by Camera drift; unlocked hands the camera to the orbit controls. (2) An enhanced look, lazily loaded when the shared toggle is on and the renderer is a real GPU: shader variants for depth fade, size attenuation and soft sprites, plus fixed-strength grade, vignette and second-bloom passes, all built once inside the existing BassInkPost composer and switched with flags.

findings.finding: C1 describes trio's band split as a pure function over one spectrum (bandLevels(spectrum, binHz, edges, out)). In the repo it is not. Each TrioColorWaveSheet creates its own AnalyserNode (trioColorWaveSheet.ts:63-69) with a per-band fftSize (1024, 2048 and 4096 in trioColorWaveConfig.ts), minDecibels and smoothing. Band edges come from user sliders (values[lowKey], values[highKey], line 110). The level is a stateful peak-normalised value (PEAK_DECAY, gain at lines 117-120). bass-ink has one analyser and none of those sliders. So S1 either needs three extra analysers in bass-ink (this contradicts the non-goal 'no new audio analysis' and adds per-frame cost) or the 'trio split' is silently approximated. The AC11 golden test would then prove nothing about what bass-ink computes, and AC3 ('split as trio-color-wave splits them') cannot be verified.
findings.suggestion: Decide before S1. Preferred: bass-ink computes its own bass, mids and highs from its existing spectrum or rhythm.state.bandOnsets, using fixed edges copied from trio's default band settings. Leave trio untouched, so AC11 is trivially true and S1 drops out of the critical path. Reword D7 and AC3 to 'trio-like band split'. If real sharing is wanted, extract only the stateless sampleLogSpectrum/blur kernel and say so in C1.
findings.resolution: User chose trio-like: stateless trio helpers move to a shared module (C1, AC11 golden test); bass-ink reads three bands from its one analyser with trio's default edges. No new analysers. D7, AC3 reworded.

findings.finding: D6, C2 and AC10 assume a camera orbit that composes with OrbitControls, drag, lock and reset. The shared createOrbitView (app/lib/three/orbitView.ts) exposes only setLocked, reset and dispose. It has no dragging state and no per-frame update hook. OrbitControls re-derives its spherical state from camera.position on every update, so an external yaw offset gets absorbed into the controls. onViewChanged compares camera.position to the default, so an auto-moving camera would make the 'view changed' flag and the reset button misreport. reset() only restores default position and target, not the plan's yaw offset. The existing code deliberately rotates the cloud object, not the camera, 'to keep the orbit's reset position' (useBassInkScene.ts:496). C2's `dragging` flag and 'after controls update' (K3) have no source. Fixing this in orbitView would touch three other visualizers.
findings.suggestion: Rotate the cloud, core, dust and spray group, as the drift already does, and keep the camera under OrbitControls. 'Camera orbit' then means the picture turns. Derive dragging from pointerdown and pointerup on renderer.domElement inside bass-ink, not from a shared change. Rewrite D6 and AC10 to say so, and add a unit test that reset zeroes the offset and that the 'view changed' flag is not tripped by the auto-rotation.
findings.resolution: User pointed to the dancer: camera written only while locked, unlocked hands it to orbit controls, reset and relock zero the angle; shared orbitView untouched. D6, AC10, C2 rewritten.

findings.finding: The new rotation is forced on every standard-mode user and overlaps the existing motion: drift += cameraDrift*driftSpeed (line 497), viewSwing, and cloud.object.rotation (line 501). The code states that 'a still view stays still' at cameraDrift 0 (line 499). AC3 requires a floor drift in silence. AC10 only says 'the existing camera drift control still works'. Unresolved: does drift 0 disable the auto-orbit, do the two add, and does a user who set drift to 0 now see motion with no control to stop it? Camera lock is the only off switch, and it also blocks dragging. This is the one change that reaches the whole standard audience, and it is called 'the only standard-mode change'.
findings.suggestion: Make the auto-orbit scale with, or be gated by, the existing cameraDrift control: drift 0 means no auto-yaw, the default means the floor..cap range. State this in AC3 and AC10, and add a unit test. Otherwise add an explicit control and say that the default is a visible change for all users.
findings.resolution: User chose: Camera drift scales the orbit, drift 0 means no orbit (D10, AC3).

findings.finding: Slice order and contract freezing are weak. C3 (attach(post, materials)) depends on the unverified origin/main toggle (K1) and on BassInkPost internals. Yet S3 'starts by reading the real store' and C3 is already marked frozen. S2 and S3 both edit useBassInkScene.ts, and C4 is split across S2, S3 and S5, with `enhancedActive` appended after the orbit columns. S4 edits the shared shaders in inkCloud.ts and dustField.ts. Uniform or shader changes there reach the standard path and software renderers, and nothing tests that toggle-off output is unchanged (AC1 only covers the rotation).
findings.suggestion: Add an S0 that checks out origin/main, records the real toggle API and freezes C3 and C4 (including column order). Merge S2 and S3 serially. In S4, make the enhanced shader paths separate variants or defines. Add a test that the default uniforms and the compiled standard program are identical with enhanced off.
findings.resolution: Added S0 to verify the toggle and freeze C3 and C4 with column order; S3 depends on S2 so edits are serial; shader variants via a define; AC12 tests the standard program is unchanged.

findings.finding: The afterimage trails are screen-space and default to 0.4 (bassInkControls). A continuously rotating view, fastest in loud music, smears the whole cloud into arcs, and enhanced mode adds a second bloom on top. The plan evaluates neither the smear nor the legibility of formations and sprays under rotation. K6 only covers the depth fade. Spray is emitted in the cloud's local space (useBassInkScene.ts:505-508), so a rotating group changes where bursts appear on screen.
findings.suggestion: Add a manual and screenshot check at cap speed with default trails to S2. Define the cap by the maximum per-frame angular step, or reduce the afterimage damp in proportion to the rotation speed (a constant, not a music-driven value). Record the outcome in Q1.
findings.resolution: Max per-frame angular step in C2, manual cap-speed smear check in S2, K7 and Q1.

findings.finding: AC2 ('shows the enhanced layers (richer shading, depth and extra post)') and the success metric 'judged clearly more stunning' have no observable check. AC8's 'mid-range laptop GPU' is undefined and cannot run in CI, since CI uses SwiftShader (Q2 admits enhanced may not render there at all). K2's fallback ('drop the second bloom first') is a manual decision, not a runtime guard. The request is 'as visually stunning as possible', yet O4 is a static fog, grade, vignette and second bloom plus soft sprites. It reads closer to O1 than to a stunning result, and the plan cannot show it clears the bar.
findings.suggestion: Name the reference device and tool for AC8 (e.g. the GPU frame time query or the dev telemetry frame time). Make AC2 observable: enhancedActive telemetry equals 1, the pass count is N, and named uniforms are set. Require before and after screenshots on a real GPU as S4 evidence. Add an automatic quality step-down if the rolling frame time is over budget (resolution scale, not a pass swap, per bassInkPost.ts:74-77).
findings.resolution: AC2 made observable (telemetry, pass flags, define, screenshots); AC8 uses dev telemetry on the user's reference GPU (Q3) with an automatic render-scale step-down; K8 for the stunning bar.

findings.finding: AC4 and C3 say toggling swaps passes in place with no context loss. bassInkPost.ts:74-77 states 'never switch the render path on a slider change', and the afterimage is reallocated when trails return (lines 86-94). Adding or removing composer passes and half-res targets at runtime means new shader compiles and render-target allocation on the toggle frame (a hitch). Late-resolving imports and the existing trails re-creation add race paths. 'Dispose restores the standard uniforms' is hard to verify with the fake renderer used in the unit tests.
findings.suggestion: Build the enhanced passes once on load, kept disabled, and toggle .enabled so the swap is a flag flip. Free them only on scene dispose. Add a test that toggle, trails-off and trails-on, then toggle again does not double-free or leak the afterimage.
findings.resolution: Build once and flip enabled flags (D12, C3); test toggle with trails off and on in between.

findings.finding: AC1 plans to regenerate the bass-ink standard baseline 'only for the rotation'. A yaw integrated over elapsed time makes any screenshot time-dependent. In CI (silent, SwiftShader) the angle at capture would be the floor speed times load time, which makes the snapshot flaky. The plan does not say how the angle is frozen for the visual spec. e2e/visual.spec.ts iterates VISUALIZERS_UNDER_TEST, so bass-ink is likely covered.
findings.suggestion: Add to S2/S5: the visual spec runs with a deterministic rotation (angle 0 / reduced-motion emulation or a test hook), and the baseline diff is reviewed as rotation-only.
findings.resolution: Visual spec freezes the orbit through reduced-motion emulation, which stops it (AC6), so the baseline is deterministic.

findings.finding: AC6 ends with 'damped to a slow, level-independent drift or stopped', which is two outcomes, so it is not testable. The plan does not say how prefers-reduced-motion is read, whether it is live (matchMedia change) or fixed at mount, or whether it reaches the pure orbit module.
findings.suggestion: Pick one outcome. Read it with matchMedia and a change listener, and pass it in through the C2 flags. Add a unit test for a mid-play change.
findings.resolution: AC6 now one outcome: stopped; read live with matchMedia and passed to C2 (D11).

findings.finding: The riskiest assumptions are D8/K1 (the toggle API is as planned, rated medium likelihood but never checked even though origin/main is one fetch away) and 'the orbit's reaction cells are unchanged' (K5, rated low). K5 is plausible for audio-side signals, but the pointCount, fit and swing code read the camera. D9's R2 is honest, but the dependence on F1's wrong premise makes S1 and AC11 the weakest-grounded parts of the plan.
findings.suggestion: Verify the toggle on origin/main now, before approval, and put the actual store path and hook signature in the plan. Run debug:viz on bass-ink before S2 to get a baseline that K5 can be compared against.
findings.resolution: Cannot run git in planning; S0 verifies the toggle on origin/main first and records a debug:viz baseline; K5 raised to medium.
